finding.statement: The scene contains several world scales, but the render gives no explicit camera-scale transition between them.
finding.impact: The bounded habitat reads as a static diagram: the viewer can see the floor, agent ring, and task rings, but is not cued when the visual focus expands from workers to the larger task field.

candidate_change.atomic_change: Insert one 0.6-second camera pull-back immediately before the task-orbit reveal at the current line 97 transition (after the worker pulses and before Create(task_orbits)). Hold the wider framing through the receipt end state.
candidate_change.implementation_intent: Use a single calibrated zoom-out, approximately 0.80 of the current camera zoom, without changing source data, object radii, colors, labels, or overlay placement.
candidate_change.success_condition: The pull-back visibly establishes the nested relationship between the 35-tile bounded field, the agent ring, and all three task orbits while keeping the fixed title, live counts, task text, receipt label, and footer legible.

evidence.observation: The camera orientation and focal_distance=22 are set once; no later camera transform or zoom call exists in the scene.
The habitat floor is a 7 by 5 grid (35 tiles) spanning x=-6..6 and z=-4..4.
Agent positions use radii 2.10, 2.48, and 2.86; task orbits use radii 3.70, 4.25, and 4.80. These scale layers are encoded but not introduced by a framing cue.

Measured render metadata: 854x480, 15 fps, 172 frames, 11.466016 seconds. Sampled frames 30, 60, 90, 120, 150, and 171 retain the same camera perspective while content is added; there is no visible pull-back at the task-orbit reveal.

falsifier: Reject this finding and candidate if a source or frame-level inspection shows an existing camera zoom/framing change at the task-orbit transition, or if the current render already communicates the three scale layers without a framing transition.

next_measurement.procedure: Render the candidate at the same 854x480/15 fps settings. Compare consecutive frames across the 0.6-second pull-back and sample the pre-transition, transition midpoint, task-orbit reveal, and final frames.
checks: Projected worker-node diameter decreases monotonically during the pull-back.
All 35 floor tiles, 15 agent nodes, and 3 task orbits remain inside frame bounds after the move.
Fixed-frame title, counts, task text, receipt label, and footer do not scale or move with the world.
The wider final framing remains stable through the receipt end state.
